_about: Phases 03 and 04 — Production and Post-production. NOT produced by npm run extract: the 2023 pages this app was migrated from stopped at the tech recce, so there is no legacy source to parse. Same schema as steps.feature.json so renderSteps() handles both with no new code. Checklist-heavy on purpose: a shoot day is not a writing prompt, it is a list you work through before the light goes.

production.title: The Shoot Day.
production.deck: Pre-production was deciding. Production is protecting those decisions from the weather, the clock and everyone's good ideas at 4pm.

blocks.label: WHY THIS MATTERS
blocks.body: A day is lost in the first ninety minutes or not at all. Crews that start late never catch up, because the shots you drop are always the last ones on the list — and the last ones on the list are the ones you needed for the cut.
blocks.tanglish: Kaalaila late aana, andha naal poidum. Kadaisila drop panra shot thaan edit la romba theva padum.

items.label: A · The first shot of the day, and why it is first
items.placeholder: The setup that unlocks the rest of the day…

items.label: B · What you will drop if you are two hours behind
items.placeholder: Decide this now, in daylight, not at 7pm with the crew watching.

items.text: Call sheet issued the night before, not the morning of.
Every HOD has read the day's shot list, not just received it.
The drop-order is written down and the AD knows it.
Batteries, cards and a second monitor cable are on the truck.

production.title: The Continuity Log.
production.deck: The only department whose mistakes cannot be fixed in post without money. Write it down while you can still see it.

blocks.label: 96 · CRAFT LESSON
blocks.trade: A timeline you can follow without being told
blocks.body: 96 moves between school and the reunion constantly, and you are never lost — because costume, hair and light change on a rule, not a whim. Continuity is not pedantry; it is what lets an audience track two decades without a caption.
blocks.tanglish: 96 la school-um reunion-um maara maara varum, aana confuse aagadhu — costume, hair, light ellam oru rule padi maarudhu.

items.label: A · Your continuity rule for time (what changes when the period changes)
items.placeholder: Costume palette, hair length, lens, grade…

items.label: B · Who holds the log, and where it lives
items.placeholder: Name, and the folder everyone can reach.

items.text: Stills of each costume and prop position before the first take.
Screen direction noted for anything that will cut together.
Watches, phones and food levels checked between takes.
Scene, slate and take logged against the breakdown.

production.title: The Dailies.
production.deck: Watch what you actually shot, not what you meant to shoot. The gap between the two is the film you are really making.

blocks.label: WHY THIS MATTERS
blocks.body: A missing reaction shot costs an hour on the day and a week in the edit. Dailies exist so that the day you can still reshoot is the day you find out.
blocks.tanglish: Reaction shot miss aana, andha naal oru mani neram; edit la oru vaaram. Adhaan dailies.

items.label: A · What is missing from today that you can still get
items.placeholder: Coverage, a reaction, a clean exit…

items.label: B · Where the day's footage is backed up, in two places
items.placeholder: Drive A / Drive B — and who checked the copy.

items.text: Two copies of the day's card, verified — not just copied.
Sound and picture from the same take can be found together.
Tomorrow's call sheet reflects anything that slipped today.

production.title: The Wrap.
production.deck: The shoot ends. The obligations do not. Close them while people still answer your calls.

items.label: A · What is still owed — people, locations, equipment
B · The pickup list you are honest about
items.placeholder: Shots you will need and must schedule, not hope for.

items.text: Every crew member's payment date is agreed in writing.
Locations released and returned to condition, with photos.
All footage and sound consolidated and checked off the breakdown.
Cast release forms signed — every speaking part, no exceptions.

post.title: The Assembly.
post.deck: Everything, in order, too long. Resist the urge to make it good before you make it whole.

blocks.label: WHY THIS MATTERS
blocks.body: An assembly that is honest about its length tells you what the film is. Trimming before you have seen the whole thing means cutting scenes for being slow when the real problem is three scenes later.
blocks.tanglish: Full-a paakaama cut panna, thappana scene-a vettiduven — problem munnadi illa, appuram irukkum.

items.label: A · Assembly runtime, and your target
B · The three weakest stretches, watched cold

items.text: Every scene from the breakdown is in the timeline, or deliberately cut.
Watched start to finish in one sitting, without stopping to fix.
Notes taken as a viewer first, an editor second.

post.title: The Picture Lock.
post.deck: The cut stops moving so that sound, music and colour can start. A lock that keeps slipping costs all three departments twice.

blocks.label: VIKRAM VEDHA · CRAFT LESSON
blocks.body: Vikram Vedha's nested stories only work because each one lands on a reversal. In the edit that is unforgiving: shorten the wrong beat and the reversal arrives before the audience has taken the bait. Lock the structure, then trim inside it.
blocks.tanglish: Ovvoru kadhaiyum oru reversal la mudiyanum. Thappana idathula vetti-na, twist varradhukku munnadiye audience purinjiduvaanga.

items.label: A · Lock date, agreed with sound and music
B · What could still force a change, and who decides
items.placeholder: Be specific. "Notes" is not an answer.

items.text: Watched with an audience who have not read the script.
Every temp shot is either final or flagged for VFX with a date.
Reel lengths and timecode handed to sound in their format, not yours.

post.title: The Sound & Music.
post.deck: Half the film, made last and budgeted first to be cut. Protect it: an audience forgives a soft image and never forgives muddy dialogue.

blocks.label: WHY THIS MATTERS
blocks.body: Dialogue you cannot hear is a scene the audience leaves. Everything else in the mix — score, ambience, effects — exists to serve the line, and the mix is where a film that was working stops working, quietly.
blocks.tanglish: Dialogue kekkala na, andha scene-e poidum. Mix la thaan padam nalla irundhadhu kettu poidum.

items.label: A · Which scenes need re-recording, and who is available
B · The music brief in one sentence
items.placeholder: What the score must do that the picture cannot.

items.label: C · Mix format and where it will be heard

items.text: Every line is intelligible on a laptop speaker, not just in the studio.
Music cues are cleared, credited and paid for — including any samples.
A mix checked at low volume, which is how most people will hear it.
M&E track delivered, for any dub or territory later.

post.title: The Delivery.
post.deck: Colour, titles, captions, masters. The unglamorous fortnight that decides whether anyone can actually play your film.

items.label: A · The grade in one reference
items.placeholder: A film, a photograph, a time of day.

items.label: B · Who needs what, in which format
items.placeholder: Festival DCP, streamer ProRes, press stills, subtitle file…

items.label: C · First screening, and the date you are working towards

items.text: Subtitles checked by someone who speaks both languages well.
Credits verified against every release form and payment.
A master archived somewhere that is not your editing drive.
The file actually played, start to finish, on the device it will be shown on.
